# The admission fixture (10 §15.3 "Admission", B1-r1 10). Every sequencer assigns these actions these ticks:
# src/shared/admission.ts (test/shell/admission.test.ts) and the native TestSequencer (the sim package).
#
#   case <name>                                   starts a case; ticks restart, the open tick is 1
#   open <tick>                                   the open tick: the earliest an action may join
#   act <player> <seq> <payload bytes> <blob count> -> <tick>
#   run <player> <first seq> <count> <payload bytes> <blob count> -> <tick>:<n> [<tick>:<n> …]
#                                                 `count` actions with consecutive seqs; the first n go to the
#                                                 first tick, the next to the second …
# Player 65535 is the system player (its seq is the system seq). Limits: CLOSURE_MAX = 1,048,576 bytes and a
# 4,096-byte system reserve, so a player's action fits while both sizes stay within 1,044,480. Closure size:
# 16 per batch (a new batch at a change of player or a gap in seqs) + 4 + payload per action. Wire size:
# 17 + 32 × blobs + payload per action.

case small actions share the open tick
open 1
act 0 1 6 0 -> 1
act 0 2 3 0 -> 1
act 1 1 12 0 -> 1
act 65535 1 4 0 -> 1
act 0 3 2 0 -> 1

case a later open tick
open 41
act 0 7 6 0 -> 41
act 0 8 6 0 -> 41

case a full tick spills to the next and closes to players; system actions use the reserve
# 15 actions of 65,531 bytes in one batch: closure 16 + 15 × 65,535 = 983,041, wire 15 × 65,548 = 983,220.
# The 16th would make the closure 1,048,576 > 1,044,480: it and every later player action go to tick 2.
run 0 1 17 65531 0 -> 1:15 2:2
act 65535 1 4 0 -> 1
act 1 1 6 0 -> 2
act 65535 2 4 0 -> 1

case blobs fill the wire before the closure
# Each action: wire 17 + 32 + 36 = 85, closure 4 + 36 = 40 (+16 for the batch). 12,288 × 85 = 1,044,480 fits
# exactly; the next goes to tick 2.
run 3 1 12290 36 1 -> 1:12288 2:2

case consecutive seqs share a batch
# Fifteen actions alternating players 0 and 1, each its own batch: closure 15 × 65,551 = 983,265, wire
# 15 × 65,548 = 983,220. Player 0's next seq continues its batch (closure + 4 + 61,211 = 1,044,480 exactly).
act 0 1 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 1 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 2 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 2 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 3 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 3 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 4 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 4 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 5 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 5 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 6 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 6 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 7 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 7 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 8 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 9 61211 0 -> 1

case a gap in seqs starts a batch
# As above, but player 0's next action skips a seq (one the sequencer dropped): its batch header no longer fits.
act 0 1 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 1 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 2 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 2 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 3 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 3 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 4 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 4 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 5 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 5 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 6 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 6 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 7 65531 0 -> 1
act 1 7 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 8 65531 0 -> 1
act 0 10 61211 0 -> 2

case a player's actions never go earlier than its previous one
# Player 2's large action spills to tick 2 and closes tick 1; its small next one follows it to tick 2, and so
# does every other player's action.
run 2 1 15 65531 0 -> 1:15
act 2 16 65531 0 -> 2
act 2 17 1 0 -> 2
act 4 1 1 0 -> 2
